## 5. Project Scope & Research Question

+ **What is the primary research question(s) you aim to answer using this data?** (Be specific).
    + To what extent do travel distance, franchise strength, and home-court advantage influence NBA game outcomes, and can these factors be combined into a simple model that predicts game results?
+ **Which specific variables from your dataset will be most important for answering your research question(s)?**
    + All above mentioned variables seem important for our analyses. As we progress with our research will most probably have some adjustements.
+ **Briefly outline your initial ideas for analysis.** (e.g., specific graphs, statistical tests, models you might use).
    + High level idea and purpose of our research
    
        + Our goal is to see how travel distance, franchise strength, and home-court advantage influence NBA game outcomes, and whether combining these factors can help us make simple, reasonable predictions. Each factor reflects something real about team performance, so together they may provide a clear way to estimate which team is more likely to win.
        + To evaluate our approach, we will use data from 2023–2024 to build our factor scores and then predict the outcomes of 2025 games. Since we already know the actual 2025 results, we will measure our prediction accuracy by comparing our predicted winners to the real winners and computing the percentage of games we got right.

    + Travel Distance Factor
        + To analyze travel distance, we will merge our game data with the distance table to measure how far each away team traveled. Then we will group games by distance and compare win rates for short, medium, and long trips. This will give us a distance impact score that shows whether long travel makes teams more likely to lose, and we will use this as one of our prediction factors.
      
    + Franchise Strength Factor
        + To measure franchise strength, we will standardize each player’s game performance using league-wide z-scores and combine these into a single performance index. Averaging this index for each franchise gives us a franchise strength score, which shows whether a team has a positive, neutral, or negative effect on player performance and serves as one of our prediction factors.
      
    + Home-Court Advantage Factor
        + To measure home-court advantage, we will compare each team’s win rate at home versus away and visualize the differences with ggplot2. This will give us a home-advantage factor showing how much playing at home increases the chance of winning, which we will include in our final prediction model.
    
    + Desired Outcome
      + Once we understand how each factor influences game results, we will turn them into simple numerical scores that can be added together. Each factor (distance, franchise strength, and home advantage) will get a small positive or negative value based on how strongly it affects winning. For example, if long travel lowers the chance of winning, it might get a negative score, while strong franchises and home-court advantage might get positive scores. Adding these small values together will give us a final prediction score for each team, which we can use to guess the winner of a game.
